notes: Accept. 332 items — the largest extraction in the batch — with 12 library, 260 planned and 60 missing, every missing item routed exactly once. I reproduced both hashes the source block records: the LaTeX e-print (4a732681…) and the PDF (c1fe1cd8…) of arXiv 2010.00657v3. Having the same source file made three checks possible that are usually out of reach. First, the statuses: all 57 distinct planned layer ids exist, and the five source routes land in layers named for this theorem (IntegralIwasawaTheory I.6/I.7 are 'Integral Brumer–Stark prerequisites' and 'The integral Brumer–Stark theorem'). Thirty planned items are named by two routes each; no missing item is, so section 16 is satisfied and the doubling is the deliberate 'a source route may also name planned items' pattern. Second, the twelve library items: twenty of their twenty-two citations match declarations.tsv exactly, and the two that do not are index artefacts, not errors — HenselianRing.is_henselian is a class field (Henselian.lean:96) and IsAdicComplete.henselianRing is an instance written with a priority (Henselian.lean:170), neither of which index_declarations.py can capture; both are in Mathlib at the pin, and I read them. The declarations behind the less obvious claims say what is claimed: TauCeti.subgroupCharSum is ∑_{h∈H} χ(h)h, TauCeti.AuslanderReitenTranspose is the cokernel of Hom(P₀,A) → Hom(P₁,A), and Rep.indCoindIso is Ind ≅ Coind for a finite-index subgroup. Third, the claim that the paper contains no mistakes: I ran a mechanical audit of the LaTeX source, and it is clean — 283 labels with none duplicated, 257 cross-references with none undefined, no cross-reference whose word disagrees with its environment, and no leftover editing markers (the two apparent hits are \DeclareMathOperator{\red}{red} and the bibliography's \begin{thebibliography}{XXX}). That is evidence for an empty sourceIssues list, not proof: it is not a line-by-line re-reading of a 100-page paper. One defect of my own finding, reported rather than rewritten: the locators' auxiliary source-line numbers drift. Every one of the 230 labels they cite resolves in the file the extraction hashes, so no item is misattributed and the section and statement names are exact; but the line numbers run ahead of the true ones by an amount that grows through the file — \label{c:rubin} is at 405 against a cited 421, t:main at 511 against 539, l:abab at 685 against 726, and by line 3440 the drift is about 7.5%. The pattern is what reading a soft-wrapped copy would produce. Since every locator also carries its label, the fix for a reader is to use the label; rewriting 222 locators mechanically would have left mixed conventions, so I left them and recorded the measurement here. Nothing else was corrected, and nothing was rejected or deleted.
